before.stem: ww Regarding the female urethra, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The urethra is longer in women than it is in men. 1%
The urethra begins at the apex of the bladder. 10%
The urethra opens in the vestibule that lies between the labia minora.
The inferior aspect of the urethra is bound to the posterior surface of the vagina. 4%
The internal urethral sphincter surrounds the urethra as it passes through the pelvic floor. 13%
before.explanation: In women the urethra is short (about 4 cm long), beginning at the base of the bladder. It passes inferiorly through the urogenital diaphragm into the perineum before opening in the vestibule that lies between the labia minora. The inferior aspect of the urethra is bound to the anterior surface of the vagina and the urethral opening is anterior to the vaginal opening in the vestibule. The external urethral sphincter surrounds the urethra as it passes through the pelvic floor. 7 v

after.stem: Regarding the female urethra, which of the following statements is CORRECT:

The urethra opens in the vestibule that lies between the labia minora.
The inferior aspect of the urethra is bound to the posterior surface of the vagina.
The internal urethral sphincter surrounds the urethra as it passes through the pelvic floor.
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The short female urethra opens into the vestibule between the labia minora; its inferior aspect is related to the anterior, not posterior, vaginal surface.

before.stem: A 29 year old man presents to ED with a painful lump in his left groin. Which of the following structures can be used to differentiate between a direct and an indirect inguinal hernia:
before.explanation: A direct inguinal hernia (in contrast to an indirect inguinal hernia) does not pass through the deep inguinal ring but directly through the posterior wall of the inguinal canal, through the lower portion of the inguinal triangle which is bordered laterally by the inferior epigastric vessels. Therefore an indirect inguinal hernia is lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, but a direct inguinal hernia is medial to these vessels. , Vv

after.stem: A 29 year old man presents to ED with a painful lump in his left groin. Which of the following structures can be used to differentiate between a direct and an indirect inguinal hernia:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: Indirect hernias lie lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, whereas direct hernias lie medial to them.
after.learningNote: Indirect hernias lie lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, whereas direct hernias lie medial to them.
after.highYieldNote: Indirect hernias lie lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, whereas direct hernias lie medial to them.
after.mnemonic: Indirect is lateral; direct is medial to epigastrics.

memoryAid.coreFact: Indirect hernias lie lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, whereas direct hernias lie medial to them.
memoryAid.mnemonic: Indirect is lateral; direct is medial to epigastrics.

evidence.externalFinding: Source explanation directly supports the inferior epigastric landmark.

before.stem: ww The inferior vena cava lies posterior to which of the following parts of the duodenum:
options: Second part (x) hird and fourth parts 1% (v’) First and third parts 20%
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The superior (first) part extends from the pyloric orifice of the stomach to the neck of the gallbladder, lies just to the right of the body of vertebra L1, and passes anterior to the inferior vena cava and superior to the head of the pancreas.
